s: A company is building a software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution on AWS. The company has deployed an Amazon API Gateway REST API with AWS Lambda integration in multiple AWS Regions and in the same production account. The company offers tiered pricing that gives customers the ability to pay for the capacity to make a certain number of API calls per second. The premium tier offers up to 3,000 calls per second, and customers are identified by a unique API key. Several premium tier customers in various Regions report that they receive error responses of 429 Too Many Requests from multiple API methods during peak usage hours. Logs indicate that the Lambda function is never invoked. What could be the cause of the error messages for these customers?
o: The Lambda function reached its concurrency limit.
The Lambda function its Region limit for concurrency.
The company reached its API Gateway account limit for calls per second.
The company reached its API Gateway default per-method limit for calls per second.

w.y: Lambda is never invoked, so API Gateway is throttling the requests itself. Several premium customers, each allowed up to 3,000 RPS across multiple methods, can together exceed the account-level API Gateway throttle quota (10,000 RPS per Region by default), which returns 429. The quota is shared by all APIs in the account in that Region.

o.A: Lambda concurrency throttling happens at invocation, but the logs show Lambda was never invoked.
o.B: Same problem: a Regional Lambda concurrency limit would appear as Lambda throttles, not requests rejected before invocation.
o.C: Correct: the per-Region account-level API Gateway throttle is shared across all APIs and keys, so it returns 429 before the integration runs.
o.D: There is no separate default per-method limit. Method throttles exist only if you configure them, and errors across many methods point to the account limit.

s: Throttle requests to your REST APIs for better throughput in API Gateway
